title: Sign of the Cross
when: At the start and end of every prayer, and when entering a church with holy water.
text:
In the name of the Father,
and of the Son,
and of the Holy Spirit.
Amen.
meaning: With a simple gesture, touching forehead, chest, left shoulder and right shoulder, we name the Trinity: one God in three Persons. It recalls our baptism, which was done "in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit" (Matthew 28:19), and marks us with the cross of Christ.

title: Our Father
when: At every Mass, in the Rosary, and any time of day.
text:
Our Father, who art in heaven,
hallowed be thy name;
thy kingdom come,
thy will be done
on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us this day our daily bread,
and forgive us our trespasses,
as we forgive those who trespass against us;
and lead us not into temptation,
but deliver us from evil.
Amen.
meaning: This is the prayer Jesus himself taught his disciples when they asked, "Lord, teach us to pray" (Luke 11:1). We call God "Father" because Jesus invites us to share his own relationship with the Father. The prayer asks first for God's glory and kingdom, then for what we need: daily bread, forgiveness, and protection from evil.

title: Hail Mary
when: In the Rosary, the Angelus, and personal prayer.
text:
Hail Mary, full of grace,
the Lord is with thee.
Blessed art thou among women,
and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
Holy Mary, Mother of God,
pray for us sinners,
now and at the hour of our death.
Amen.
meaning: The first half repeats the words of the angel Gabriel and of Elizabeth to Mary (Luke 1:28 and 1:42). The second half asks Mary to pray for us, the way we might ask a friend to pray for us. Catholics do not worship Mary; we honor her as the mother of Jesus and ask her prayers.

title: Glory Be
when: After the psalms, at the end of each decade of the Rosary, and as a short prayer of praise.
text:
Glory be to the Father,
and to the Son,
and to the Holy Spirit,
as it was in the beginning,
is now, and ever shall be,
world without end.
Amen.
meaning: A short prayer of praise to the Trinity. It says that God's glory has no beginning and no end.

title: Apostles' Creed
when: At the start of the Rosary, and in many prayers; it is a summary of what Christians believe.
text:
I believe in God, the Father almighty,
Creator of heaven and earth;
and in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord,
who was conceived by the Holy Spirit,
born of the Virgin Mary,
suffered under Pontius Pilate,
was crucified, died, and was buried.
He descended into hell;
on the third day he rose again from the dead;
he ascended into heaven,
and is seated at the right hand of God the Father almighty;
from there he will come to judge the living and the dead.
I believe in the Holy Spirit,
the holy catholic Church,
the communion of saints,
the forgiveness of sins,
the resurrection of the body,
and life everlasting.
Amen.
meaning: One of the oldest summaries of the Christian faith, used in baptism since the early Church. Its three parts follow the Trinity: God the Father who creates, Jesus Christ who saves, and the Holy Spirit who gives life to the Church.

sources.title: Catechism of the Catholic Church, Part One: The Profession of Faith

title: Act of Faith
when: Any time, especially in the morning or when faith feels weak.
text:
O my God, I firmly believe
that Thou art one God in three Divine Persons:
the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
I believe that Thy Divine Son became man,
and died for our sins,
and that He shall come to judge the living and the dead.
I believe these and all the truths
which the Holy Catholic Church teaches,
because Thou hast revealed them,
Who canst neither deceive nor be deceived.
Amen.
meaning: Faith, hope and love are the three "theological virtues": gifts that come from God and lead back to him. This prayer says yes to the heart of what Christians believe: the Trinity, Jesus who became man, died and will come again. We believe not because we have worked it all out, but because we trust the God who reveals it.

title: Act of Hope
when: Any time, especially in worry or discouragement.
text:
O my God, relying on Thy almighty power
and infinite mercy and promises,
I hope to obtain pardon of my sins,
the help of Thy grace, and life everlasting,
through the merits of Jesus Christ,
my Lord and Redeemer.
Amen.
meaning: Hope is trust that God will keep his promises: forgiveness, help for today, and life with him forever. It does not rest on how well we are doing, but on God's power and mercy, and on what Jesus has already done for us.

title: Act of Charity (Love)
when: Any time, especially when it is hard to forgive.
text:
O my God, I love Thee above all things,
with my whole heart and soul,
because Thou art all-good and worthy of all love.
I love my neighbor as myself for the love of Thee.
I forgive all who have injured me,
and ask pardon of all whom I have injured.
Amen.
meaning: "Charity" is the old word for love. Jesus said the greatest commandments are to love God with all your heart and your neighbor as yourself (Matthew 22:37-39). This prayer puts both into words, and adds the hardest part: forgiving others and asking their forgiveness.

title: Morning Offering
when: First thing in the morning.
text:
O Jesus, through the Immaculate Heart of Mary,
I offer Thee all my prayers, works, joys, and sufferings of this day
for all the intentions of Thy Sacred Heart,
in union with the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass throughout the world,
in reparation for all my sins,
for the intentions of all our associates,
and in particular for the special intentions of our Holy Father for this month.
Amen.
meaning: A way to give your whole day to God before it starts, so that ordinary work and even hard moments become a prayer.

title: Another Morning Offering
when: In the morning. Based on Our Lady of Fatima's requests.
text:
O Jesus, through the Immaculate Heart of Mary,
I offer Thee all my prayers, works, joys, and sufferings
and all that this day may bring:
for the love of Thee,
for the conversion of sinners,
and in reparation for the sins committed
against the Sacred Heart of Jesus
and the Immaculate Heart of Mary.
Amen.
meaning: A shorter way to give the whole day to God. Whatever comes, good or hard, becomes a gift offered out of love and for others who need God.

title: Prayer to your Guardian Angel
when: Morning and evening.
text:
Angel of God, my guardian dear,
to whom God's love commits me here,
ever this day (night) be at my side,
to light and guard, to rule and guide.
Amen.
meaning: The Church teaches that each person has an angel watching over them (see Matthew 18:10). This short prayer asks for that angel's help through the day.

title: Grace Before Meals
when: Before eating.
text:
Bless us, O Lord, and these thy gifts,
which we are about to receive from thy bounty,
through Christ our Lord.
Amen.
meaning: A short thank-you to God for food, often said with the Sign of the Cross.

title: Grace After Meals
when: After eating.
text:
We give Thee thanks, Almighty God,
for these and all Thy benefits,
Who livest and reignest forever.
Amen.

May the souls of the faithful departed,
through the mercy of God, rest in peace.
Amen.
meaning: We thank God before eating and again after. The second line remembers those who have died, because Catholics keep praying for loved ones even after death.

title: Act of Contrition
when: In the sacrament of confession, and at night before sleep.
text:
O my God, I am heartily sorry
for having offended Thee,
and I detest all my sins
because I dread the loss of Heaven and the pains of Hell;
but most of all because they offend Thee, my God,
Who art all good and deserving of all my love.
I firmly resolve, with the help of Thy grace,
to confess my sins, to do penance,
and to amend my life.
Amen.
meaning: A prayer telling God we are sorry for our sins and want to change. There are several versions; your priest will accept any sincere words of sorrow. Ask your parish which version they teach.

title: The Confiteor (I Confess)
when: At the start of Mass in the Penitential Act, and in personal prayer.
text:
I confess to almighty God
and to you, my brothers and sisters,
that I have greatly sinned,
in my thoughts and in my words,
in what I have done
and in what I have failed to do,
through my fault, through my fault,
through my most grievous fault;
therefore I ask blessed Mary ever-Virgin,
all the Angels and Saints,
and you, my brothers and sisters,
to pray for me to the Lord our God.
Amen.
meaning: Confiteor is Latin for "I confess." At Mass we say it together, which reminds us that sin is never only private: it touches the whole family of God, and so we ask that family, in heaven and in the pews, to pray for us. At "through my fault" many people gently strike their chest.

title: The Memorare
when: In any need. A famous prayer associated with St. Bernard of Clairvaux.
text:
Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary,
that never was it known
that anyone who fled to thy protection,
implored thy help,
or sought thy intercession
was left unaided.
Inspired with this confidence,
I fly unto thee, O Virgin of virgins, my Mother.
To thee do I come, before thee I stand,
sinful and sorrowful.
O Mother of the Word Incarnate,
despise not my petitions,
but in thy mercy hear and answer me.
Amen.
meaning: Memorare is Latin for "Remember." We come to Mary as children come to their mother, confident she will bring our needs to her Son. Catholics do not worship Mary; we ask her to pray for us, the way we ask friends to pray for us.

title: The Angelus
when: At 6 am, noon and 6 pm throughout the year, except during the Easter season.
text:
V. The Angel of the Lord declared unto Mary,
R. And she conceived of the Holy Spirit.
Hail Mary...

V. Behold the handmaid of the Lord.
R. Be it done unto me according to Your Word.
Hail Mary...

V. And the Word was made flesh,
R. And dwelt among us.
Hail Mary...

V. Pray for us, O holy Mother of God.
R. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

Let us pray:
Pour forth, we beseech You, O Lord,
Your Grace into our hearts;
that as we have known the incarnation of Christ,
your Son, by the message of an angel,
so by His passion and cross
we may be brought to the glory of His Resurrection.
Through the same Christ, our Lord.
Amen.
meaning: The Angelus remembers the moment God became man: the angel's message to Mary, her yes, and the Word made flesh (Luke 1:26-38; John 1:14). Church bells traditionally ring at these hours so people can pause wherever they are. "V." is said by a leader and "R." is the response; alone, you say both.

title: The Regina Caeli
when: At 6 am, noon and 6 pm during the Easter season, in place of the Angelus.
text:
V. Queen of Heaven, rejoice, alleluia.
R. For He whom you did merit to bear, alleluia.
V. Has risen, as he said, alleluia.
R. Pray for us to God, alleluia.
V. Rejoice and be glad, O Virgin Mary, alleluia.
R. For the Lord has truly risen, alleluia.

Let us pray:
O God, who gave joy to the world
through the resurrection of Thy Son,
our Lord Jesus Christ,
grant we beseech Thee,
that through the intercession of the Virgin Mary, His Mother,
we may obtain the joys of everlasting life.
Through the same Christ our Lord.
Amen.
meaning: Regina Caeli means "Queen of Heaven." From Easter Sunday to Pentecost, the Church replaces the Angelus with this joyful prayer, sharing with Mary the joy that her Son is risen.

title: O My Jesus (Fatima Prayer)
when: After the Glory Be in each decade of the Rosary. Requested by Our Lady of Fatima in 1917.
text:
O my Jesus, forgive us our sins,
save us from the fires of hell,
lead all souls to heaven,
especially those in most need of thy mercy.
Amen.
meaning: A short prayer for mercy, associated with the appearances of Mary at Fatima, Portugal, in 1917. Many people add it to each decade of the Rosary.

title: Hail, Holy Queen
when: At the end of the Rosary.
text:
Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy,
our life, our sweetness and our hope.
To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve;
to thee do we send up our sighs,
mourning and weeping in this valley of tears.
Turn, then, most gracious advocate,
thine eyes of mercy toward us;
and after this our exile,
show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

Pray for us, O holy Mother of God,
that we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
Amen.
meaning: An ancient prayer (in Latin, the Salve Regina) asking Mary, as a loving mother, to bring us to her Son. It closes the Rosary.

title: Prayer After the Rosary
when: At the end of the Rosary, after the Hail, Holy Queen.
text:
O God, Whose only begotten Son,
by His life, death, and Resurrection,
has purchased for us the rewards of eternal salvation,
grant, we beseech Thee,
that meditating upon these Mysteries
of the Most Holy Rosary of the Blessed Virgin Mary,
we may both imitate what they contain
and obtain what they promise.
Through the same Christ Our Lord.
Amen.
meaning: The Rosary is not only repeating words: it is thinking about Jesus' life with Mary. This closing prayer asks that what we just pondered would change how we live.

title: Most Sacred Heart of Jesus
when: A short prayer for any moment, often said three times.
text:
Most Sacred Heart of Jesus,
have mercy on us.
Most Sacred Heart of Jesus,
have mercy on us.
Most Sacred Heart of Jesus,
have mercy on us.
meaning: The Sacred Heart is a sign of Jesus' human and divine love for each person. This tiny prayer can be said anywhere: on a walk, in traffic, in a hard moment.

title: O Sacrament Most Holy
when: Before the Blessed Sacrament, or when passing a church.
text:
O Sacrament most holy,
O Sacrament divine!
All praise and all thanksgiving
be every moment Thine!
meaning: Catholics believe Jesus is truly present in the Eucharist. This short verse is a way to greet him, for example when you visit a church and see the tabernacle with its lit candle.

title: Jesus, Mary, and Joseph
when: Any time, and especially when praying for a good death.
text:
Jesus, Mary, and Joseph,
I give Thee my heart and my soul.
Jesus, Mary, and Joseph,
assist me in my last agony.
Jesus, Mary, and Joseph,
may I breathe forth my soul in peace with Thee.
Amen.
meaning: The Holy Family is a model for every family. St. Joseph is the patron of a happy death because, tradition says, he died with Jesus and Mary beside him.

title: Sacrifice Prayer
when: Whenever you make a small sacrifice. Our Lady of Fatima asked that it be said often.
text:
O my Jesus, I offer this for the love of Thee,
for the conversion of sinners,
and in reparation for sins committed
against the Immaculate Heart of Mary.
meaning: A small sacrifice, like skipping a treat or being patient instead of snapping, can become a prayer when you offer it to God for others.

title: Eternal Rest
when: For those who have died, at any time and especially in November.
text:
Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord,
and let perpetual light shine upon them.
May the souls of all the faithful departed,
through the mercy of God, rest in peace.
Amen.
meaning: Love does not end at death. Catholics pray for the dead, trusting God to finish his work of mercy in them. November is the month the Church especially remembers them.

title: Prayer to St. Michael
when: Any time, especially in temptation or trouble.
text:
St. Michael the Archangel,
defend us in battle;
be our safeguard against the wickedness and snares of the devil.
May God rebuke him, we humbly pray,
and do thou, O Prince of the heavenly host,
by the power of God,
cast into Hell Satan and all the other evil spirits
who prowl about the world,
seeking the ruin of souls.
Amen.
meaning: Written by Pope Leo XIII, this prayer asks the archangel Michael, who in Scripture fights against evil (Revelation 12:7), to protect us.
